title: a device answers a verb addressed to a machine it holds
intention: A device answers a verb addressed to a machine it holds, machines/<machine>/<verb>, by handing the envelope to that machine's own declared verb, so a ticket can ask devices/codemother/0/machines/<gate>/queueme <fileref>.
why: Outline 3.3.4.3 and 9.6 (Akien 2026-11-10, Q#80 and Q#81 answers): a ticket crosses a gate by asking devices/codemother/0/machines/<inspector>/queueme <fileref>, and each chart stage and the verdict is a gate machine answering queueme. Measured 2026-11-10: BaseDevice.declared_verbs (cairn/tools/base/device.py:186) is a flat table of show and get, so no device can answer a verb addressed to one of its machines.
traces_to: RULE 1 (a device is reached through its public interface, the bus); outline 3.3.4.3; the recursive verb shape (verbs descend into more precise direction, like the CLI).
how: BaseDevice gains declared_machines() -> {name: machine}, default {}; each machine exposes declared_verbs() -> {verb: callable(envelope) -> dict}. BaseDevice.declared_verbs() adds 'machines/<name>/<verb>' for every held machine verb, so the shim's existing lookup (cairn/tools/base/shim.py:869), its bounce and its announce menu carry them with no shim change. A red-first proof drives a fixture shim with a spy bus.

clauses.claim: a fixture device declaring machine 'gate_x' with verb 'queueme' has 'machines/gate_x/queueme' in declared_verbs(), and a shim delivering an envelope with that verb calls the machine's handler with the envelope and posts its answer with reply_to equal to the request id
an envelope with verb machines/no_such/queueme bounces, its reason naming the declared verbs, which include machines/gate_x/queueme
an envelope with verb machines/gate_x/no_such bounces the same way and the machine's handler is not called
the announce menu the shim posts at wiring lists machines/gate_x/queueme
a held machine whose name or verb contains '/' makes declared_verbs() raise ValueError naming it, and a device that declares no machines answers exactly show and get as before

decisions.text: D1: in cairn/tools/base/device.py add BaseDevice.declared_machines(self) -> dict returning {} with a docstring citing outline 3.3.4.3, and change BaseDevice.declared_verbs() to return {'show': ..., 'get': ..., **self._machine_verbs()}, where _machine_verbs() walks declared_machines().items(), raises ValueError(f"machine {name!r} verb {verb!r}: a name or verb may not contain '/'") when either contains '/', and maps f'machines/{name}/{verb}' to the machine's handler. The machine object needs only a declared_verbs() method; a machine without one raises TypeError naming it.

D2: the proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_device_answers_a_verb_for_a_machine_it_holds.py, red-first, PROVES 15d850266972 clauses 1 to 5, one tooth each. It copies the _SpyBus and fixture-shim shape of cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_raising_handler_still_answers.py: a fixture BaseDevice subclass whose declared_machines() returns {'gate_x': _Gate()}, _Gate.declared_verbs() returning {'queueme': handler recording the envelope and returning {'accepted': True, 'queued': fileref}}. Tooth 4 calls the shim's _announce_menu and reads the posted body's verbs.

out: any device declaring machines (CodeMother's gate machines are their own ticket)
the ticket machine and its queueme call (their own ticket)

measured.saw: BaseDevice.declared_verbs returns only show and get; shim.deliver resolves a verb by dict lookup over declared_verbs()
the six devices with verb tables of their own (cairn, codemother, harbor_master, inference_domain, librarian, tester) all spread **super().declared_verbs()
